newsitem.title: UK: Emerging market debt focus on FOMC, eye e.Europe.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt focus on FOMC, eye e.Europe.

text.p: Emerging market debt was subdued on Friday after a hectic week and some dealers said cautiousness ahead of the early July U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting would limit trade next week.
"We've seen good strength in the market overall this week," ANZ assistant director Chris Portman said.

"The market is going to be somewhat nervous ahead of the FOMC meeting, but the Fed is unlikely to raise rates which is a positive backdrop for the Brady market and once we get past the FOMC meeting we see further gains," Portman added.
A recent string of soft economic data coupled with some political pressure would deter the Fed from raising short-term interest rates at the July 1-2 meeting, economists said in a Reuters poll.
All but one of 36 analysts polled on Tuesday and Wednesday said the central bank would leave the federal funds rate unchanged at 5.50 percent.
The economists said that with jobs in abundance and low inflation, there would not be any justification for an interest-rate hike at this time.
Meanwhile with some saying Latin American Brady bonds were more dictated by U.S. interest rates, the focus on Russian and Bulgarian risk continued, dealers said.
Russian MinFin bonds rose amid optimism about Russia's new heavily-oversubscribed Eurobond and Moscow's plans to close an agreement with the London Club of commercial creditors.
Added to this the Duma has approved the new tax code.
BankAmerica analyst Richard Gray said: "The most interesting one is Russia.
"Should there be 'flippers' -- buyers in and out of the new 10-year bond -- investors are buying the longer end of the Minfin curve to position themselves should flipping occur," he said.
Russia's Minfin 7 was bid at 41.875 at 1100 GMT and the Russian Vnesh US$ at 91.625.
Also from eastern Europe, progress towards the introduction of the currency board in Bulgaria continued to buoy bonds although there was some light profit-taking, dealers said.

"Spreads on Bulgaria IABs have now compressed by over 150 basis points in the past two weeks and 585 b.p. since the turn of the year," ANZ investment bank said in its weekly emerging market debt commentary.
At 1100 GMT Bulgaria FLRB were bid at 57.250, Bulgaria IAB at 72.500 and Bulgaria DISC at 74.250.
